figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Self-resistance gene guided genome mining combined with activity screening identiﬁes a novel family of ClpP inhibitors. a) Workﬂow for
self-resistance gene guided genome mining approach used to identify ClpP-associated clusters from genomes available in GenBank and in-house
database. b) Gene cluster sequences obtained through genome mining were used to construct an SSN with BiG-SCAPE, followed by network
visualization and annotation using Cytoscape. c) Partial biosynthetic gene clusters obtained from genome mining. d) Representative structures of
known ClpP inhibitors or activators from actinomycetes, including the inhibitors clipibicyclene and cystargolides A and B, and the activator ADEP1. e)
Examples of hits from the screening using the Suc-LY-AMC peptidase assay via ﬂuorogenic assay, including the crude extracts of Streptomyces sp.
S186 and A. inagensis DSM 44258. f) Crude extract of Streptomyces sp. S186 can inhibit the antibacterial activity of ADEP1.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Discovery, biosynthesis, and bioengineering of streptoclipamides as ClpP-targeting proteolysis inhibitors. a) Chemical structures of 1–7
from Streptomyces sp. S186. b) Architecture of str BGC in BAC p5N18. Genes involved in biosynthesis are labeled with distinct colors, while unrelated
ORFs remain uncolored. c) Determination of the inhibitory activity of compound 1 on ClpP via ﬂuorogenic assay (n = 3). d) Compound 1-mediated
inhibition of ADEP antibacterial activity against MRSA and MRSA persisters. e) Proteolytic activity inhibition by compound 1 against housekeeping
ClpP (Orf654), and resistant ClpP enzymes StrM and StrN (n = 3). f) HPLC analysis of M6-fermented culture extracts of wild-type and engineered
strains: wild-type Streptomyces sp. S186 i), S. coelicolor M145 harboring pMSBBAC1 ii), S. coelicolor M145 harboring p5N18 iii), mutant strains
p5N18strJiv), p5N18strK v), and S. coelicolor M145 harboring pJTU2554-B7 (strA–strO CRISPR-Cas9 construct) vi). g) Accumulated products (8–12)
from S. coelicolor M145/p5N18 mutant strains.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Incorporation of acetate units conﬁrmed by 13C-labeling experiments and proposed PKS/NRPS hybrid biosynthetic pathway for
streptoclipamides. a) [1-13C] acetate feeding studies conﬁrmed C2-unit incorporation into compound 1 via 13C NMR analysis, revealing speciﬁc
enrichment at C-1, C-8, C-29, C-31, and C-33. b) Proposed biosynthetic pathway of streptoclipamides. Domain abbreviations: acyl carrier protein
(ACP), acyltransf erase (AT), ketosynthase (KS), ketoreductase (KR), dehydratase (DH), peptidyl carrier protein (T), adenylation (A), condensation
(C), thioesterase (TE).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Streptoclipamide A (1) inhibits ClpP protease without bactericidal activity and modulates virulence factor production. a) Inhibition of
compounds 1–12 (IC50) against MRSA USA300 ClpP proteolytic activity (n = 3). NA indicates no activity. b) Growth curves of MRSA USA300 treated
with 1 (16–500 µM) compared to DMSO control (n = 3). c) RT-qPCR analysis of expression levels of clpP, RNAIII, agrA, sarA, saeR, hla, psmα, lukE,
lukF-PV, lukS-PV, fnbA, spa, clfA and srtA in the presence of compound 1 (100 µM) (n = 3). The functions of these targeted genes are listed in
Table S5. d) Dose-dependent inhibition of MRSA USA300 hemolytic activity by compound 1 and Western blot analysis of α-hemolysin (Hla)
expression (n = 3). e) Eﬀect of diﬀerent concentrations of compound 1 on the hemolysis activity of MRSA USA300 (EC50 = 32.79 µM) (n = 3).
f) Determination of the neutralization activity of compound 1 on pre-formed Hla in the supernatant of MRSA USA300 (n = 3). g) Inhibitory activity of
compound 1 on proteolysis of MRSA USA300 (EC50 = 79.84 µM) (n = 3). Signiﬁcance is calculated based on one-way ANOVA: ns P > 0.05,
** P ≤0.01 and **** P ≤0.0001.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. Direct binding of streptoclipamide A (1) to ClpP. a) TSA showing compound 1-induced Tm of ClpP protein. b) CETSA analysis of
compound 1-ClpP binding by SDS-PAGE. c) SPR analysis of compound 1-ClpP binding kinetics. The chromatic lines represent the kinetic signal
response to the binding interaction. d) The predicted binding mode of ClpP from the molecular docking simulations. e) Tm values comparison of
ClpP treated with compounds 1–12 (16 µM, n = 4). f)–h) Compound 1-induced Tm in ClpP mutants: T72A (f), T72P (g), M95A (h). i) WT-ClpP and
ClpP mutants were incubated with or without compound 1 (1.6 µM), and the hydrolytic activity of recombinant ClpP. j) Sequence alignment of ClpP
homologs reveals a key resistance-conferring T72P substitution in StrM. Signiﬁcance is calculated based on one-way ANOVA: **** P < 0.0001. All
experiments presented were repeated three times.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 6. Streptoclipamide A (1) alleviates the pathogenic eﬀect of MRSA USA300 on G. mellonella and mice. a) Schematic overview of the G.
mellonella infection and treatment protocol using MRSA USA300 and compound administration. b) Survival curves of G. mellonella larvae (n = 15)
over 5 days following infection and treatment. Signiﬁcance is calculated based on one-way ANOVA: ns P > 0.05, * P ≤0.05, *** P ≤0.001 and ****
P ≤0.0001. c) Images of G. mellonella larvae from all treatment groups (n = 15 per group) at 120 h post-infection. d) Bacterial burden in lung tissues
of mice 48 h after intranasal infection with MRSA USA300 and subsequent treatment. CFU per gram of lung tissue is shown as scatter plots with
median values (n = 6). * P ≤0.05, ** P ≤0.01, *** P ≤0.001 and **** P ≤0.0001. e) Gross morphology and histopathological examination (H&E
staining) of mouse lungs from each treatment group, revealing the extent of inﬂammation and tissue damage.
